claims.text: The feedstock is homogeneous gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle size of 10–60 μm.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder is dispersed in an acrylate-based photocurable resin and DLP-printed into layered green bodies.
Continuous mechanical-pump evacuation creates an oxygen-deficient debinding environment.
Oxygen-deficient debinding decreases oxidation of the resin.
Oxygen-deficient debinding decreases oxidation of the alloy powder.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retains residual carbon in regions formerly occupied by resin.
Residual carbon in former resin regions reduces pore volume.
Reduced oxidation limits rapid gas evolution during debinding.
In oxygen-rich debinding, oxidation of resin and powder generates CO and CO2.
Rapid escape of oxidation-generated gases produces pressure-driven surface cracks.
Oxygen-rich debinding forms deleterious oxides on particle surfaces.
Limiting gas evolution and surface-oxide formation promotes lower-temperature diffusion and interparticle bonding.
Oxygen-deficient debinding causes earlier loss of layered morphology and earlier densification during sintering.
Air-debound specimens require sintering at 1100 °C for full consolidation.
Air-debound specimens have an approximately 5.1 MPa maximum compressive strength.
Relative to air-debound specimens, oxygen-deficiently debound specimens will reach full consolidation at about 1050 °C, approximately 50 °C lower.
Oxygen-deficiently debound specimens will retain a maximum compressive strength comparable to approximately 5.1 MPa.
Oxygen-deficient debinding will improve dimensional precision relative to air debinding.
Oxygen-deficient debinding will reduce surface cracking and porosity relative to air debinding.
The predicted effects are limited to the specified DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi powder/resin system, debinding schedule, and 800–1100 °C sintering range.
